title: Grounding DINO 1.5: Advance the "Edge" of Open-Set Object Detection

problem.summary: Open-set detectors built on Grounding DINO still fall short on generalization across diverse categories, and their multi-scale features plus heavy feature enhancer make them impractical for real-time/edge deployment where compute resources are limited; early-fusion designs also trade higher recall for object hallucinations.
statements: There is a large gap between the computational cost required by an open-set detection model and the limited resources available on edge devices.
Grounding DINO's multi-scale image features and heavy feature enhancer are impractical for real-time scenarios in real-world applications.
Early-fusion training yields higher recall and box precision but can increase model hallucinations such as predicting objects not present in the input images.
Open-set detectors need stronger generalization across long-tailed and in-the-wild categories (COCO, LVIS, ODinW).

evidence.quote: However, there is a large gap between the computational cost required by an open-set detection model and the limited resources available on edge devices.

Grounding DINO uses multi-scale image features and a heavy computational feature enhancer for faster training and better performance, which is impractical for real-time scenarios in real-world applications.
However, this approach can also lead to increased model hallucinations, such as predicting objects not present in the input images.

background.summary: Extends Grounding DINO (itself built on DINO and GLIP's phrase-grounding formulation with large-scale detection+grounding pre-training and self-training on pseudo-labeled image-text pairs) and cites Lite-DETR for the observation that low-level features are costly and semantically weak; the gap claimed is a lack of both a stronger-scaling model and a genuinely efficient edge variant.

evidence.quote: This approach, coupled with self-training on pseudo-labeled grounding data derived from an almost unlimited pool of image-text pairs, enhances the model’s applicability to open-world settings due to its robust architecture and semantic-rich dataset.

A key strategy for improving model generalization across diverse object categories is the integration of language modality, which has received increasingly more attention and has undergone extensive development in recent research.

solution.summary: Grounding DINO 1.5 is a two-model suite: Pro scales the Grounding DINO architecture with a ViT-L backbone and early fusion trained on Grounding-20M (over 20M grounding-annotated images), while Edge replaces the feature enhancer with an efficient one that fuses only P5 features (vanilla self-attention plus cross-scale fusion of P3/P4) on an EfficientViT-L1 backbone, both trained on the same data.
solution.approach: Scale up an early-fusion dual-encoder/single-decoder grounding detector with a 20M-image grounding dataset, and cut edge cost by restricting cross-modality fusion to high-level features with an efficient feature enhancer.
components: deep early fusion (cross-attention between language and image features before decoding)
enhanced training sampling that increases the proportion of negative samples
Grounding-20M dataset with annotation pipelines and post-processing rules
efficient feature enhancer operating on P5 features only (Edge)
cross-scale feature fusion module integrating P3/P4 features

evidence.quote: we have upscaled the model by incorporating the pre-trained ViT-L [6] architecture and developed a data engine capable of producing over 20 million images with grounding annotations from diverse sources
we replace deformable self-attention with vanilla self-attention, and introduce a cross-scale feature fusion module [37] to integrate low-level image features (from P3 and P4 levels).
Grounding DINO 1.5 is pre-trained on over 20M grounding images, termed Grounding-20M
we have retained the early fusion design while introducing a more comprehensive training sampling strategy, which increases the proportion of negative samples during training.

experiments.summary: Evaluates Pro zero-shot on COCO, LVIS (val/minival, fixed AP) and ODinW13/35, fine-tunes Pro on LVIS and ODinW, and evaluates Edge zero-shot on COCO/LVIS with PyTorch/TensorRT FPS on A100 plus FPS on NVIDIA Orin NX, comparing against grounding and open-vocabulary detectors.

evidence.quote: the Grounding DINO 1.5 Pro model attaining a 54.3 AP on the COCO detection benchmark and a 55.7 AP on the LVIS-minival zero-shot transfer benchmark, setting new records for open-set object detection.
transfer benchmarks, Grounding DINO 1.5 Pro achieves a 55.7 AP and a 47.6 AP, outperforming the previous best model, DetCLIPv3, by 6.9 AP and 6.2 AP, respectively.

the fine-tuned Grounding DINO 1.5 Pro model achieves a 68.1 AP and a 63.5 AP on the LVIS-minival and LVIS-val splits, respectively, which represent an enhancement of 12.4 AP and 15.9 AP over the Grounding DINO 1.5 Pro zero-shot setting.
Grounding DINO 1.5 Edge achieves a zero-shot AP of 45.0 on COCO.

limitations.summary: No explicit limitations section; evident ones are the early-fusion hallucination trade-off, dependence on prompt engineering to repair poor category names in some ODinW test sets, modest Edge speed on the actual edge device at large input sizes, and offline-only video processing.
items: Early fusion increases object hallucinations; the paper only mitigates this with more negative samples.
ODinW evaluation involved prompt engineering on category names for datasets where performance was poor.
Some ODinW datasets have significant quality issues in annotated category names.
Edge model exceeds 10 FPS on NVIDIA Orin NX only at 640x640 input (about 5.5 FPS at 800x1333).
Video object detection demos are processed offline.

evidence.quote: However, this approach can also lead to increased model hallucinations, such as predicting objects not present in the input images.
We observe that within the ODinW benchmark, several datasets exhibit significant quality issues in terms of the annotated category names.
during testing, we performed prompt engineering to refine category names on datasets where their performance was particularly poor to better align their category names with actual testing scenarios.

deploymentClaims: 75.2 FPS on an NVIDIA A100 with TensorRT optimization while reaching 36.2 zero-shot AP on LVIS-minival.
Over 10 FPS on NVIDIA Orin NX at 640x640 input size with TensorRT-optimized Edge model.
Edge model designed specifically for faster speed demanded by applications requiring edge deployment.
API and demos released for practical use.

evidence.quote: the Grounding DINO 1.5 Edge model, when optimized with TensorRT, achieves a speed of 75.2 FPS while attaining a zero-shot performance of 36.2 AP on the LVIS-minival benchmark, making it more suitable for edge computing scenarios.
We deploy the model on the NVIDIA Orin NX platform, achieving an inference speed of over 10 FPS at an input size of 640 × 640.
